business.name: Ethan Construction
business.location: Southlake, TX; serves Grapevine, Keller and nearby

personal_note: Ethan, you said most of your work comes from referrals and you'd like to be found on Google. The good news: the expertise is already on your site. It just isn't being seen yet.
headline: Ethan Construction has the expertise. Let's make sure people find it.
intro: Ethan Construction already has a strong foundation: clear remodeling services, practical know-how and real local expertise. We found three opportunities to make more of what is already built.

strengths.title: Practical expertise
strengths.body: Kitchen and bathroom pages answer real homeowner questions.

strengths.title: Local knowledge
strengths.body: Southlake and Grapevine pages show genuine familiarity with the area.

strengths.title: Useful resources
strengths.body: The Material Library helps homeowners choose with confidence.

opportunities.name: Get discovered
opportunities.summary: The expertise is on the site, but Google and AI assistants barely see it.
opportunities.title: The expertise is there. It isn't being discovered yet.
opportunities.body: Ethan's website explains remodeling better than most. Yet very few people are being shown it: **the issue is visibility, not expertise.**

findings.title: Hours don't match across sources
findings.body: The website says 8–6 on weekdays; Google shows 9–5, which lowers search engines' confidence.

findings.title: Listings describe a different business
findings.body: Some directories mention commercial work, roofing and painting rather than residential remodeling.

findings.title: Links come from unrelated sites
findings.body: Most of the 466 backlinks SEMrush reports have nothing to do with remodeling.

first_steps: Make hours, services and areas identical on the website and Google.
Correct directory listings that describe commercial or roofing work.
Add structured data and answer the top ten homeowner questions.
opportunities.opportunity_title: One consistent version of Ethan across the web
opportunities.opportunity_body: Align the basics everywhere Ethan appears so homeowners, Google and AI assistants can find the expertise already on the site.

opportunities.name: Show the proof
opportunities.summary: Make finished projects as visible as the know-how.
opportunities.title: The proof should match the expertise.
opportunities.body: Remodeling is a high-trust decision. Ethan explains the work well, but completed projects and happy homeowners are hard to see.
opportunities.comparison_caption: Review count isn't quality, but it is what homeowners compare.

findings.title: Reviews aren't part of handover
findings.body: There is no routine moment where finished clients are asked for a review.

findings.title: Projects aren't shown as stories
findings.body: Before-and-after photos and the decisions behind them rarely reach the website.

first_steps: Text a review link to the last five happy clients this week.
Add a review request to the project sign-off checklist.
Publish one kitchen remodel as a short before-and-after story.
opportunities.opportunity_title: Make proof a by-product of every project
opportunities.opportunity_body: Ask for a review and capture a short project story at every handover, so proof grows with the work.

opportunities.name: Reuse every project
opportunities.summary: Capture photos, decisions and lessons once, then use them everywhere.
opportunities.title: Every project can keep creating value after it is finished.
opportunities.body: Every remodel produces photos, decisions and solutions. Most of it is useful long after the job is done.

findings.title: Knowledge stays with the crew
findings.body: How a tricky layout or material problem was solved isn't written down anywhere reusable.

findings.title: Content starts from scratch
findings.body: Marketing is created separately instead of drawing on the work itself.

example.title: A kitchen remodel in Keller
example.body: A homeowner wants a larger island. The layout, wiring and flooring decisions become a portfolio story, an FAQ answer and a sales reference.

first_steps: Create a one-page end-of-project form: photos, decisions, one problem solved.
Store each project in one shared folder, named by type and town.
Turn one finished project into a homeowner FAQ answer each month.
opportunities.opportunity_title: Capture the important parts once, reuse them
opportunities.opportunity_body: A simple end-of-project routine turns each job into material for sales, the team, search and AI.

next_steps.title: Fix the visibility foundation
next_steps.body: Align Ethan's public information and strengthen relevant authority.

next_steps.title: Make proof part of every handover
next_steps.body: Build reviews and project stories into project completion.

next_steps.title: Capture and reuse project knowledge
next_steps.body: Turn each finished job into content for customers, sales and search.

closing: Ethan already has the expertise and does the work; the opportunity is to make both work harder for the business.
